headline: Low interaction risk overall; no shared execution or data channels, but caveman’s MCP-enabled docs surface creates a small prompt-injection bridge if manually connected.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: caveman can use MCP and exposes file surfaces like CLAUDE.md/docs, while python-cheatsheet has no clipboard, stdin/stdout, files, or MCP. No default bridge is documented, so injection is not inherent; it only appears if an operator manually connects caveman outputs into another parser.
conditions: IF caveman outputs are manually copied into another agent's prompt or parser, injection becomes plausible.
IF an MCP server is attached to caveman and trusted content is not provenance-tagged, prompt injection risk increases.
mitigations: Keep the agents disconnected from shared prompts or copy-paste flows.
Disable MCP for caveman unless a specific workflow needs it.
Add a provenance prefix to any caveman-generated text before reuse.
Review any CLAUDE.md or docs content before feeding it to another agent.

B_data_leakage.rationale: caveman touches session logs, memory files, project notes, and CLAUDE.md, but python-cheatsheet has no filesystem read, no files, and no API calls. With no shared workspace or upload path documented, there is no plausible default leakage route between them.
conditions: IF both agents are placed in the same writable workspace, leakage becomes possible.
IF python-cheatsheet is wrapped by an external orchestrator that injects caveman files into its context, leakage risk changes.
mitigations: Keep separate workspaces for each agent.
Do not mount caveman memory files into python-cheatsheet.
Avoid passing session logs or project notes between agents.
Verify any orchestrator does not auto-share files across agents.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: caveman supports multiple instances, but python-cheatsheet cannot write files, modify git state, or spawn subprocesses. There is no overlapping mutable resource in the profiles, so a write-write conflict is not supported by the evidence.
conditions: IF python-cheatsheet is wrapped with additional write permissions outside this profile, conflict risk would need reevaluation.
IF both agents are later granted write access to the same directory, contention becomes possible.
mitigations: Keep python-cheatsheet read-only.
Do not grant shared git or filesystem write access.
Run caveman instances in isolated sessions.
Use an external lock if future tooling adds shared writes.

D_cascading_error.rationale: caveman can produce project notes and CLAUDE.md content, but python-cheatsheet is documentation-only and has no action-taking or API surfaces. The pair lacks a default downstream automation path, so any cascade would require an operator to treat caveman output as authoritative.
conditions: IF an operator copies caveman output into a downstream workflow as authoritative text, errors can cascade.
IF python-cheatsheet is embedded in a larger system that executes its text, the risk increases.
mitigations: Require human review before reusing caveman output.
Mark caveman output as draft or untrusted.
Keep python-cheatsheet in read-only reference mode.
Add a verification step before any downstream action.

E_compliance.rationale: Both profiles are open-source, docs-only, and list no secrets, OAuth scopes, or regulated data classes. No residency, retention, or certification mismatch is evidenced, so there is no compliance pathway to score.
conditions: IF either agent is later used with regulated data, compliance must be reassessed.
IF deployment adds retention or residency constraints not shown here, this verdict no longer applies.
mitigations: Avoid routing regulated data through either agent.
Document any future residency or retention requirements.
Reassess if OAuth scopes or secrets handling are added.
Keep both agents in documentation-only workflows.
